drhp.business: Apollo Tyres Ltd manufactures and sells automotive tyres under the Apollo Tyres and Vredestein brands. Its product portfolio spans passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, two-wheelers, off-highway vehicles, and light trucks, catering to both original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and the replacement market. The company operates manufacturing facilities in India and Europe, supported by global R&D centers and a wide distribution network.

drhp.expansion: The Company continued to invest in its modern, highly automated manufacturing facilities across India and Europe, which provide a strong foundation for cost-competitive production and support growth across both domestic and international markets. The state-of-the-art facility in Andhra Pradesh was highlighted during the Apollo Tyres Global Partners' Summit in February 2026, showcasing the scale, advanced technology, and operational discipline driving the next phase of growth. No new specific capex projects with commissioning or completion timelines were disclosed.

litigation.note: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) found the Company, along with other tyre manufacturers, to have contravened Section 3 of the Competition Act, 2002, and imposed a penalty. The Company appealed to NCLAT, which remanded the matter back to CCI. CCI has appealed to the Supreme Court. As of the report date, no penalty amount is enforceable against/payable by the Company.

risks.note: Natural rubber prices are subject to agricultural factors and other key inputs are influenced by crude oil prices, directly impacting cost structures and profitability.

Performance is influenced by macroeconomic conditions across geographies; slowdowns in Europe and North America may impact demand and exports, while trade policy shifts and geopolitical developments affect supply chains and inflation.
Global operations and dependence on imported raw materials and export markets expose the Company to adverse currency movements that may impact margins and earnings.
The tyre industry faces intense competition from global and domestic players, requiring continuous innovation, product differentiation, and cost competitiveness to sustain market position.

Evolving norms related to sustainability, emissions, and safety, along with rapid shifts such as increasing electric vehicle adoption, require continuous adaptation in product development and business strategy.
Geopolitical developments, global logistics disruptions, climate-related events, and rising input costs may impact supply continuity and increase transportation costs.
Growing threats from cyberattacks including ransomware and phishing attempts may impact business continuity and data security.
